crime.value: Armed bank robbery followed by kidnapping: a lone gunman robs a small branch bank at closing and takes a teller hostage as cover for his escape. Central question is not whodunit but whether he will escape and what he wants.
crime.quote: Her fingers fumbled opening the drawer and then were pushing money into the case.

victim.value: Marge Elliot, the bank teller — an ordinary suburban wife and mother, 'killable'/takeable simply because she was the last teller on duty at closing time and made a convenient hostage-disguise as a 'wife'
victim.quote: "Now just as carefully walk around the end of the counter and come out. Bring your purse."

closed_world.value: The locked branch bank at closing, then the confined interior of the getaway car during a long highway flight across state — a two-person sealed space with roadblocks, toll gates, gas stations and a motel as the only outside contacts
closed_world.quote: Mr. Redmon locked the door behind her, and glanced impatiently toward the last customer.

culprit_and_motive.value: The tall man in the windbreaker, a Korean War veteran trapped in a marriage and life he never chose; he robs the bank not for money but to escape the 'merry-go-round' of providing, leaving the cash to his wife
culprit_and_motive.quote: "I had to get out of it. She'll use the money until she finds a new guy to conjure it up and hand it over"

resolution.value: Marge's deliberately abandoned wristwatch in the rest-park outhouse leads police to the car; troopers chase the robber and he goes over a cliff, shot/dead — order 'restored' as Marge returns to Warren, but she weeps for her abductor
resolution.quote: "They got your watch; the men remembered the car. They're chasing him right now."

investigator.value: Marge, the hostage-victim herself, is the sole point of view — an amateur 'investigator' who both plots escape (leaving clues) and gradually uncovers the robber's motive and her own dissatisfaction
investigator.quote: She remembered her watch and yanked it off, leaving it on the seat.

red_herring.value: The robber's ordinary appearance and casual notebook-thumbing at the wall desk mislead Marge (and reader) into treating him as a routine customer; later the staged 'married couple quarrelling about split levels' misdirects the state trooper.
red_herring.quote: “If you have to have a split level, dammit, have it! But don’t expect me to like it!”

clue_fairness.value: The reader sees every escape detail as Marge does: the gun in the pocket, the wig and pink blouse disguise, the second blue car on the parking deck, the abandoned watch in the rest-park outhouse — the watch later proves to be the trace that leads police to him.
clue_fairness.quote: “They got your watch; the men remembered the car. They’re chasing him right now.”

social_world.value: Post-war American suburbia: PTA festivals, church committees, subdivisions like 'Pleasant View', split-level houses, breadwinner husbands who merely 'provide' and wives who are perpetually busy — a hierarchy of domestic obligation the robber indicts.
social_world.quote: “don’t you realize that’s all most men are doing now? Providing.”

alibi.value: No investigative alibi; instead a fabricated cover identity — the robber passes himself and his hostage off as a bickering married couple on a fishing trip, verified by license and luggage at the toll gate.
alibi.quote: “OK, Mac. License, please.” He studied the license and compared the statistics with the man

reveal_mechanic.value: Physical trace plus witness memory: the watch Marge deliberately leaves on the outhouse seat, combined with the dog-walking couple recalling the car, demonstrates the trail; the offstage gunfire and 'over the cliff' confirms his predicted end.
reveal_mechanic.quote: Outside someone was shouting, “. . .over the cliff. . .”

media_and_audience.value: The robber packages Marge's ordeal in advance as public spectacle — television heroine, newspapers, a national magazine buying her story, envy of the neighbours — while Warren insists on a return to 'normal'.
media_and_audience.quote: “You’ll be a heroine on television, in the newspapers. Maybe a national magazine will buy your story.”

investigator_wound.value: Marge, the point-of-view 'investigator' of her captor, is exploited through her own suppressed marital emptiness and lost faith — her longing to be cared for makes her complicit and finally grieving for him.
investigator_wound.quote: She wished passionately she could return to the time when she knew someone would be there to take care of things

suspect_wounds.value: The robber's wound is his own life: drafted out of college into Korea, tortured in a prison camp, returned to an automatic marriage and a life of merely 'providing.' Marge's parallel wound is a hollow marriage to Warren and a life of committee busywork.
suspect_wounds.quote: “A kid gets taken out of college and told to kill or be killed,” he said

unreliable_frame.value: Told in close third person through Marge, whose perceptions shift from terror to attraction; her own account of her marriage is self-censoring, and the robber answers direct questions ('Do you love her?') evasively.
unreliable_frame.quote: “Maybe I did love her, maybe I still do. I don’t know. It doesn’t matter. I had to get out of it.”

setting_as_constraint.value: The closed branch bank at lock-up (no other customers or staff), then the sealed interior of a moving car on a turnpike — toll gates, filling stations and rest parks are the only contact points, each surveilled by the captor so escape is impossible.
setting_as_constraint.quote: “There’s a rest park ahead,” he said. “We’ll get out and walk up and down a few minutes.”

evidence_type.value: Physical trace evidence deliberately planted by the victim: Marge's inscribed wristwatch left on the outhouse seat, combined with testimonial identification of the car by the couple with the dog.
evidence_type.quote: “They got your watch; the men remembered the car. They’re chasing him right now.”

technical_detail.value: Prison-camp joint-manipulation technique learned from a Korean guard — wrist pressure that dislocates the shoulder — used silently to control Marge in public; plus disguise craft (blonde wig, changed clothes, switched car) and sedation via sleeping pills dissolved in sweetened coffee.
technical_detail.quote: “I was in a prison camp in Korea and one of the guards taught me a kind of cute trick.”

moral_ambiguity.value: The robber is gentle, apologetic and protective toward his hostage, robbing not from greed but to escape a suffocating conformist life; he leaves the money to his wife and asks only to state his own terms. Marge, his victim, ends by weeping for him and recoiling from her husband.
moral_ambiguity.quote: She jerked away from him and buried her face in the pillow, where her abductor’s head had rested.
